observation.visible_scene: A wooden tabletop against a pale wall holds a domino setup: two large triangular pyramids of standing dominoes (left one teal-and-gray, right one pink-and-gray), a long horizontal row of standing dominoes running along the bottom edge of the frame, a central vertical column of teal/pink dominoes topped by a Y-shaped pair of diagonal branches resting between two clear acrylic barriers, a teal open-loop ('C' shape) on the left, and a small pink arch/bridge on the right. The watermark 'StayFawnTop' is fixed top-left.
visible_changes: For roughly the first two-thirds of the clip (t=0 to ~0.83 s) the whole arrangement is static: both pyramids stand fully intact, and the bottom row, the central stem, the Y-branches, the loop and the arch all hold their positions with no visible motion.

Around t=0.87–0.93 s the upper/left portions of both pyramids begin to topple: on the left teal pyramid the top and left-side dominoes lean and detach, tumbling outward to the left; on the right pink pyramid the left-side dominoes lean and fall leftward.

From ~1.0 s to the end (1.33 s) this collapse progresses continuously: more dominoes peel off the tops and inner edges of both pyramids and scatter onto the table to the left of each structure, leaving visible gaps in the previously complete triangles.

The bottom horizontal row, the central vertical stem, the Y-branches, the teal loop and the pink arch remain standing and essentially unchanged throughout the entire excerpt; no wave is seen traveling along them.
The background wall, table edge and watermark stay in identical positions across all frames, indicating no camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the pyramid topple (no contact from the branches, stem or barriers is visible within this segment reaching the pyramids).
Whether the topple continues to fully destroy the pyramids after the clip ends.
uncertain_details: The exact first frame of toppling is gradual; the lean is barely perceptible before ~0.87 s.
Whether the Y-branches or vertical stem show any sub-frame tipping is not clearly resolvable; they appear stationary.
The falling direction of the right pyramid's dominoes (leftward/inward) is observed but its cause is not shown.
